steps.en: Left atrial volume indexed to body surface area is the haemoglobin A1c of diastolic function: a slow moving record of chronic filling pressure. A single diameter misleads because the atrium enlarges asymmetrically, so the guideline method traces the atrial border in both apical views at its largest moment, just before the mitral valve opens, and indexes the volume. Above the threshold it marks diastolic dysfunction, chronic pressure load, and risk of atrial fibrillation. In India an enlarged left atrium should always raise rheumatic mitral stenosis in the differential, where the valve rather than the ventricle drives the enlargement.
Optimise the apical four chamber, then the apical two chamber, for the atrium rather than the ventricle: shorten the depth so the atrium fills the sector.
Freeze the frame just before mitral opening, when the atrium is largest after filling through systole.
Trace the atrial endocardium from annulus to annulus, excluding the appendage and the pulmonary vein mouths.
Use the biplane disks or area length method on the two traces and index the result to body surface area.
Repeat on a second beat in atrial fibrillation and average, because single beat volumes swing widely.
Read the indexed volume with Doppler and tissue Doppler before naming diastolic dysfunction.
Tracing the atrium in ventricular systole too early. Fix: Trace at true atrial end systole just before mitral opening. Earlier frames underread the volume.
Including appendage or pulmonary veins in the trace. Fix: The appendage and veins are not atrial body. Exclude them every time or the volume overreads.
Tracing atrial borders on a ventricular setup. Fix: Depth, focus and gain set for the ventricle blur the atrial wall. Reoptimise for the atrium.
Reporting an anteroposterior diameter as atrial size. Fix: A single diameter misses asymmetric enlargement, so always trace biplane volume and index it.
Left atrial volume index. 34 ml per sq m or less is normal; above 34 is enlarged. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left atrial volume
Timing of the atrial trace. Largest volume just before mitral valve opening. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification, section on left atrial volume
Role in diastolic grading. Above 34 ml per sq m is one of four markers of diastolic dysfunction. Source: ASE and EACVI 2016 diastolic function, section on left atrial volume
Athletic hearts can mildly exceed the limit with normal pressures, so read volume with Doppler.
Mitral valve disease enlarges the atrium regardless of ventricular diastole, so the diastolic algorithm does not apply there.
After cardioversion the atrium stays large for weeks while pressure has normalised, so trend it rather than reacting once.

q.en: When is the atrial frame taken?

o.en: At QRS onset with the mitral valve closed
At end systole of the ventricle
Just before mitral opening, at largest atrial size
At end diastole of the ventricle

why.en: The atrium is largest just before the mitral valve opens, after filling throughout ventricular systole.

q.en: Which indexed volume marks an enlarged left atrium?

why.en: The ASE 2015 upper reference limit is 34 ml per sq m, and the diastolic guideline uses the same cut point.

q.en: What is the correct tracing rule?

o.en: Trace the appendage inside the volume
Trace annulus to annulus excluding appendage and veins

why.en: The trace runs annulus to annulus along atrial endocardium with appendage and veins excluded, in both apical views.

q.en: A young Indian patient has a hugely enlarged atrium with a loud first sound and a mid diastolic rumble. What tops the differential?

why.en: Rheumatic mitral stenosis is common in India and enlarges the atrium through the stenotic valve itself, pairing a loud first sound with a diastolic rumble.
